en: Preface [By Long Xing]:
Since the Gautama clan perceived the stars and awakened to the Way, they have extensively expounded upon the sūtras and śāstras. Finally, the wondrous mind of nirvāṇa was entrusted to Mahākāśyapa.

By holding up a flower, the essential point was revealed; from lamp to lamp, the lineage has been transmitted in succession. When the First Patriarch came from the West, he relied solely on the direct [pointing].
Taking the realization of one's own mind and seeing its nature to achieve Buddhahood as its primary tenet, it is called the Nature School (Xingzong).

Bodhisattva Maitreya, based on the perfectly luminous consciousness he had realized, composed the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*. Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, drawing from its profound and vast depths, first composed the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-kārikā*.

Thereupon, Dharmapāla established the foundational principles, and Ci'en (Kuiji) expounded and transmitted them, resulting in the *Cheng weishi lun* (Treatise Establishing Consciousness-Only), which is supreme.
For the sake of precision, it is called the *Lakṣaṇa* School (the School of Characteristics). The Elder Shaojue of Old Hangzhou was the direct descendant of the Great Master Yunqi Lianchi;

he elucidated the full text [of the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*] in his work, the *Yiwen* (Phonetics and Meanings) of the *Vijñaptimātra*. His Dharma heir, Master Xinyi, extensively researched its profound principles.
There is the *Hexiang* (Harmonious Resonance). My late master, the Venerable Xian, was truly a disciple who had entered the inner chamber of Master Yi;

he further compiled and annotated [this work], correcting errors and supplementing what was omitted. These three collections all expound and interpret the profound meaning of Consciousness-Only (*vijñaptimātra*), serving as a precious torch for the True Reality School (*lakṣaṇatattvavāda*).
Some may say: "The myriad dharmas are mind-only, and the mind is one alone. Yet, if one investigates its source deeply, then—

Even "one" cannot be established. Now, regarding the mind-king (*citta*) and mental factors (*caitta*) discussed in the Abhidharma school, where the eight consciousnesses revolve around one another, and where the conditions of the object (*ālambana-pratyaya*) are scrutinized to the utmost subtlety—does this not run counter to the Way of Direct Pointing? I replied: "No, no.

Indeed, the shadows of the human mind are most difficult to exhaustively fathom. When the deluded mind recognizes these shadows, each shadow is a single mind, and that single mind is a single world; thus they circulate."

They give rise to one another in numbers exceeding ten trillion. Setting aside those who hold erroneous attachments and take illusions for reality—like sinking into the Weak Water or falling into the night mist, unable to emerge—even those of brilliant understanding and superior wisdom, within this Way...

Although one has already realized the Great Meaning and is called "thoroughly awakened," the subtle ignorance that flows into the ocean of nature cannot be removed by the sword of wisdom, nor can it be illuminated by the precious mirror;
it cannot be washed away or shaken by the rain of transformation or the thunder of the Dharma.
This is the cause of birth and death, through which one revolves with the kalpas—what is to be done? Out of compassion for this suffering, Maitreya and Vasubandhu [arose].

Therefore, I have composed this treatise and depicted these transformative manifestations (*nirmāṇa-bimba*) to shatter the delusions of the mental shadows and sever the roots of the eight consciousnesses.

This shall cause students to experience a rebirth after their final passing, transforming consciousness into wisdom (*vijñāna-parāvṛtti*). What were previously called "nets and cages" shall all become the most excellent monasteries of the blissful abode.
With wondrous functions and spiritual powers, the hundred dharmas will be fully perfected. Thus, the essential purport of the *Lakṣaṇa* school is precisely...
The thorough elucidation of distinctions serves to complement the school of the Dharma-nature, just as two axles for a chariot or two wings for a bird—how could either be neglected?
This carving of the *Weishi buyi* (Supplement to Consciousness-Only) has rendered profound service to the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye; it is no small matter.
Now that the carving is complete, I have thus inscribed this at the beginning of the scroll.
On an auspicious day in the first month of summer in the Wuma year of the Kangxi era,
